Office of Science User Facilities One important reason for establishing America’s national laboratory system immediately after World War II was to provide a home for large-scale, costly scientific facilities that universities could not afford. Such facilities were believed to be essential to sustaining America’s effort in science. The construction and operation of large-scale scientific user facilities have been integral to the mission of the DOE Office of Science from the earliest days. Today, we maintain and operate 28 DOE Office of Science user facilities at DOE national laboratories across the country as shared resources for the scientific community, with access determined on a competitive basis using peer review. Tens of thousands of researchers make use of these facilities each year. These facilities—including advanced supercomputers, particle accelerators, large x-ray light sources, neutron scattering sources, specialized facilities for nanoscience and genomics, and others—have become increasingly vital tools of scientific discovery. pages.text: Office of the Pardon Attorney | About the Office Skip to main content About the Office Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email The Office of the Pardon Attorney has long supported the American public’s ability to pursue second chances through clemency for those who have been convicted of federal offenses. In 2025, the Office expanded our mission to include supporting the American public’s ability to request federal firearm rights restoration for those who are prohibited from owning or possessing firearms under federal law. Clemency We investigate applications submitted to the Department of Justice and make recommendations to grant or deny those applications based on the standards written in the Justice Manual . pages.text: Office of the Pardon Attorney | Frequently Asked Questions Skip to main content Frequently Asked Questions Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email What is executive clemency and what does it do? What is a pardon? What is a commutation of sentence? In the federal system, pardon and commutation of sentence are different forms of executive clemency, which is a broad term that applies to the President’s constitutional power to give leniency to persons who have committed federal crimes. A pardon is an expression of the President’s forgiveness and can be granted in recognition of the applicant’s acceptance of responsibility for the crime and established good conduct for a significant period of time after conviction or completion of sentence. It removes unpaid or unserved portions of the sentence, if any, that may remain at the time the pardon was issued. It also removes civil disabilities – e.g., restrictions on the right to vote, hold state or local office, or sit on a jury – imposed because of the conviction for which pardon is sought, and should lessen the stigma arising from the conviction. It does not signify innocence. It also does not end non-criminal civil proceedings—e.g., civil forfeitures or civil IRS or SEC actions—but it may be helpful in obtaining licenses, bonding, or employment. Under some – but not all – circumstances, a pardon can eliminate the legal basis for removal or deportation from the United States. pages.text: Office of the Solicitor General | About the Office Skip to main content About the Office Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email The task of the Office of the Solicitor General is to supervise and conduct government litigation in the United States Supreme Court. Virtually all such litigation is channeled through the Office of the Solicitor General and is actively conducted by the Office. The United States is involved in approximately two-thirds of all the cases the U.S. Supreme Court decides on the merits each year. The Solicitor General determines the cases in which Supreme Court review will be sought by the government and the positions the government will take before the Court. The Office's staff attorneys, Deputy Solicitors General and Assistants to the Solicitor General, participate in preparing the petitions, briefs, and other papers filed by the government in the Supreme Court. The Solicitor General conducts the oral arguments before the Supreme Court. Those cases not argued by the Solicitor General personally are assigned either to an Assistant to the Solicitor General or to another government attorney. The vast majority of government cases are argued by the Solicitor General or one of the office attorneys. Another responsibility of the Office is to review all cases decided adversely to the government in the lower courts to determine whether they should be appealed and, if so, what position should be taken. Our Mission OVW provides federal leadership in developing the nation's capacity to reduce violence against women and administer justice for and strengthen services to victims of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, and stalking. OVW was created in 1995 and administers financial and technical assistance to communities across the country as they work to support victims, hold offenders accountable, and end domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, and stalking. Program Resources Contact Us If you have questions about the Special Tribal Criminal Jurisdiction Reimbursement Program (Tribal Reimbursement Program), you can email us or call 202-307-6026. The Tribal Reimbursement Program reimburses Tribal governments for expenses incurred in exercising Special Tribal Criminal Jurisdiction (STCJ) over non-Indians who commit certain "covered crimes" on Tribal lands. The Violence Against Women Act Reauthorization Act of 2022 (VAWA 2022) recognized the inherent power of Tribes to exercise STCJ. VAWA 2022 also established a pilot program under which the Attorney General may designate up to five Alaska Tribes per calendar year as participating Tribes to exercise STCJ over all persons present in the Tribe’s village. Learn more about STCJ . VAWA 2022 authorized this program to reimburse participating Tribes for expenses incurred in exercising STCJ. After consulting with Tribes, OVW issued implementing regulations for the program - Read the implementing regulations . What Crimes Are Covered by This Program? VAWA 2022 defines STCJ covered crimes as: Assault of Tribal justice personnel Child violence Dating violence Domestic violence Obstruction of justice Sexual violence Sex trafficking Stalking Violation of a protection

pages.text: Oficina de Normas de Gestión Laboral | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Oficina de Normas de Gestión Laboral La Oficina de Normas de Gestión Laboral (Office of Labor-Management Standards, u OLMS, por sus siglas en inglés) pertenece al Departamento de Trabajo de los Estados Unidos y es responsable de administrar y aplicar la mayoría de las disposiciones de la Ley de Notificación y Divulgación Gestión Laboral (Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act, o LMRDA, por sus siglas en inglés). Dicha ley fue adoptada con el fin de garantizar normas básicas de democracia y responsabilidad fiscal en las organizaciones laborales del sector privado. Los sindicatos que representan a los empleados del Correo Postal de los Estados Unidos también se hallan sujetos a la LMRDA. Los sindicatos de empleados federales se hallan sujetos a normas similares conforme a la Ley de Reforma del Servicio Civil de 1978 (Civil Service Reform Act, o CSRA, por sus siglas in inglés) y a la Ley del Servicio Exterior de 1980. La OLMS anima a que los oficiales y los miembros del sindicato, así como otros individuos afectados por la LMRDA, se pongan en contacto con la agencia para discutir de problemas, presenten quejas u obtengan información sobre la LMRDA. Además, la OLMS fomenta la conformidad voluntaria con la LMRDA al informar a oficiales del sindicato y a otros individuos de sus responsabilidades y al animar a los miembros del sindicato a que ejerzan sus derechos.
